objectives: This course provides a space to strengthen your English speaking skills with a particular focus on developing critical thinking and analytical abilities in spoken language. In-class work will center on student-led group presentations and discussions, both in small groups and as a class, grounded in weekly assigned texts as well as related materials and issues that students bring to the class. These texts serve not only to enrich vocabulary but also to provoke questions through which we reflect upon our assumptions and to communicate our thoughts and ideas on these important matters of historical and socio-cultural significance. Throughout the semester, students are expected to practice speaking more effectively and persuasively in English, while also developing cultural sensitivities across various socio-historical contexts. At the same time, students will learn to identify the central arguments of individual articles, the perspectives that inform them, and the stakes at play. By engaging closely with these readings, students will be asked to develop their own arguments, questions, and critiques. A central aim of the course is to prepare students for the next level of academic and professional presentation.
